evidence.claim: Reuters described Benjamin Diokno as a two-time budget minister who would lead Marcos's economic team, Arsenio Balisacan as returning as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla as incoming central bank governor, indicating a technocratic core for the new administration.
evidence.title: Factbox-Key figures in Philippine President Marcos' administration
evidence.excerpt: Reuters described Benjamin Diokno as a two-time budget minister who would lead Marcos's economic team, Arsenio Balisacan as returning as planning chief, and Felipe Medalla as incoming central bank governor, indicating a technocratic core for the new administration.
evidence.source_locator: search result excerpt under Benjamin Diokno, Arsenio Balisacan, and Felipe Medalla
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters factbox with named appointments and role descriptions; independent and specific to the 2022 transition.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers pre-inauguration 2022 appointments that shaped the target-year economic team.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos's cabinet choices.
contrary_evidence: Competence is inferred from resumes, not proven by 2022 outcomes.
The broader cabinet still mixed technocrats with political figures.

evidence.claim: Before Marcos took office, BSP raised the policy rate to 2.25 percent and projected 2022 inflation above target at 4.6 percent, citing food, energy, and supply pressures.
evidence.title: Monetary Policy Report May 2022
evidence.excerpt: Before Marcos took office, BSP raised the policy rate to 2.25 percent and projected 2022 inflation above target at 4.6 percent, citing food, energy, and supply pressures.
evidence.source_locator: Monetary Policy Summary and Economic Outlook
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official monetary policy report with explicit forecast and policy action.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited baseline only; not attributable to Marcos.
contrary_evidence: This source predates Marcos's June 30 inauguration.
It reflects inherited inflation pressures rather than Marcos policy.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that BSP raised rates by 75 basis points off-cycle to contain broadening inflationary pressure and rescue a faltering peso.
evidence.title: Philippine central bank hastens interest rate rise, ready for more action
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that BSP raised rates by 75 basis points off-cycle to contain broadening inflationary pressure and rescue a faltering peso.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a specific, dated policy action and motive.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: monetary policy was central-bank action, but it responded to the macro environment the Marcos administration faced.
contrary_evidence: The move was by the independent central bank, not the president directly.
It shows crisis management more than a Marcos-originated policy.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022 and that continuity of growth- and investment-supporting policies was key to strengthening recovery.
evidence.title: Philippines Economic Updates
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the Philippines was poised to grow 5.7 percent in 2022 and that continuity of growth- and investment-supporting policies was key to strengthening recovery.
evidence.source_locator: June 2022 entry on the economic updates page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent multilateral growth forecast and policy assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly baseline and partly policy-continuity advice; not a direct score of Marcos's implementation.
contrary_evidence: Growth forecast was based on domestic recovery conditions that predated the administration.
The report also notes external and global uncertainty.

evidence.claim: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.title: NEDA to flesh out development agenda for addressing constraints to inclusive growth
evidence.excerpt: NEDA said the Marcos administration's 8-point socioeconomic agenda would address short-term inflation and shock vulnerability, and longer-term job creation, infrastructure, logistics, energy, digitalization, regulation, and governance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official release quoting NEDA's implementation agenda and priorities.
contrary_evidence: It is an agenda statement, not implementation.
The source is official and promotional.

evidence.claim: Marcos's economic managers said the 8-point socioeconomic agenda aimed to cut poverty to 9 percent by the end of the six-year term and raise the Philippines to upper-middle-income status by 2028.
evidence.title: PH socioeconomic agenda presented at IMF, World Bank meeting
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's economic managers said the 8-point socioeconomic agenda aimed to cut poverty to 9 percent by the end of the six-year term and raise the Philippines to upper-middle-income status by 2028.
evidence.source_locator: lead paragraph and agenda bullet list
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated report on official targets announced by the administration.
contrary_evidence: Aspirational target, not observed outcome.
The source is a government newswire.

evidence.claim: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that his administration would fight food-price spikes by increasing production and supporting consumers' purchasing power.
evidence.title: Marcos relays food production agenda in 1st SONA
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said agriculture would be one of the main drivers of growth and employment and that his administration would fight food-price spikes by increasing production and supporting consumers' purchasing power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential directive within the target year, reported on an official agency page.
contrary_evidence: The source is self-reporting and policy intent, not implementation.
The food-price problem was partly inherited and global.

evidence.claim: The Marcos administration's first approved appropriations law increased funding for education, agriculture for food security, health, labor and employment, tourism, public works, and energy.
evidence.title: Senate approves 2023 national budget on third reading
evidence.excerpt: The Marcos administration's first approved appropriations law increased funding for education, agriculture for food security, health, labor and employment, tourism, public works, and energy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific budget allocation with executive attribution and concrete sectoral priorities.
evidence.period_fit: Passed in 2022 as the first budget under Marcos for FY2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level; implementation follows later.
contrary_evidence: Budget approval does not prove spending quality or execution.
Some increases mainly continue existing programs.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the Philippines needed to ease FDI restrictions and address skills and connectivity gaps, noting that amendments to the Foreign Investments Act, Retail Trade Liberalization Act, and Public Service Act were relevant to attracting investment.
evidence.title: Deeper Participation in Global Value Chains Will Strengthen Recovery and Competitiveness of the Philippine Economy
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the Philippines needed to ease FDI restrictions and address skills and connectivity gaps, noting that amendments to the Foreign Investments Act, Retail Trade Liberalization Act, and Public Service Act were relevant to attracting investment.
evidence.source_locator: middle paragraphs on structural constraints and reforms
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent policy analysis with a concrete reform list and clear period fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: the reforms were partly inherited or legislative, but Marcos's administration was responsible for implementation and promotion in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The report also makes clear that structural constraints persisted.
Some reforms were inherited rather than originated by Marcos.

evidence.claim: DOF said the Marcos administration had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to make PPPs more attractive and to secure domestic and foreign investment.
evidence.title: Marcos admin streamlines private sector participation processes to encourage investments
evidence.excerpt: DOF said the Marcos administration had streamlined private-sector participation through amended investment laws and revised BOT rules to make PPPs more attractive and to secure domestic and foreign investment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific administration policy and implementation step, dated in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct at the administration level, though the law changes partly built on prior reforms.
contrary_evidence: The source is official and promotional.
Implementation benefits were projected, not yet fully evidenced.

evidence.claim: DOF said the Marcos administration's MTFF included real-property valuation reform to broaden the tax base and promote a just, equitable, and efficient valuation system.
evidence.title: DOF unveils fiscal priority reforms under Marcos admin
evidence.excerpt: DOF said the Marcos administration's MTFF included real-property valuation reform to broaden the tax base and promote a just, equitable, and efficient valuation system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Explicit reform text tied to the administration.
contrary_evidence: Proposed reform only; not proof of enactment or anti-corruption impact.
The source is a ministry announcement.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said poverty reduction gains were substantial but inequality remained high, with the top 1 percent capturing 17 percent of national income and the bottom 50 percent receiving only 14 percent.
evidence.title: PHILIPPINES: Reducing Inequality Key to Becoming a Middle-Class Society Free of Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said poverty reduction gains were substantial but inequality remained high, with the top 1 percent capturing 17 percent of national income and the bottom 50 percent receiving only 14 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent distributional evidence with concrete shares.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2022 distributional context for Marcos's first months.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited baseline and structural conditions; useful as context for the trajectory the administration inherited.
contrary_evidence: The report also credits sustained growth, education, jobs, and social assistance for earlier poverty reduction.
The data are not a direct measure of Marcos-specific 2022 outcomes.

evidence.claim: PSA said StatDev 2022 showed the Philippines made progress on some development goals, with only four of 15 sectoral chapters at average performance and six of nine core indicators meeting targets.
evidence.title: PSA releases the 2022 Statistical Indicators on Philippine Development
evidence.excerpt: PSA said StatDev 2022 showed the Philippines made progress on some development goals, with only four of 15 sectoral chapters at average performance and six of nine core indicators meeting targets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistical synthesis with year-specific targets and outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mixed: combines inherited conditions and Marcos-year implementation; not a direct causal estimate.
contrary_evidence: The same summary says many indicators were still off track.
It is an aggregate planning metric, not a ruler-specific causal estimate.

evidence.claim: Marcos's first executive order abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and transferred its functions to the Office of the Deputy Executive Secretary for Legal Affairs in the name of bureaucracy simplification.
evidence.title: Marcos' 1st edict abolishes PACC, Office of CabSec
evidence.excerpt: Marcos's first executive order abolished the Presidential Anti-Corruption Commission and transferred its functions to the Office of the Deputy Executive Secretary for Legal Affairs in the name of bureaucracy simplification.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a dated executive order and its terms.
contrary_evidence: The administration said the move was to streamline duplicated functions, so the anti-corruption meaning is contested.
The PACC was itself a relatively new and executive-controlled body.

evidence.claim: Analysts said the PCGG should not be abolished during Marcos's rule because of conflict-of-interest concerns and the unresolved Marcos ill-gotten-wealth cases.
evidence.title: Gov't told not to abolish PCGG during Marcos rule
evidence.excerpt: Analysts said the PCGG should not be abolished during Marcos's rule because of conflict-of-interest concerns and the unresolved Marcos ill-gotten-wealth cases.
evidence.source_locator: article lead and quoted analyst comments
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reporting on a live policy debate with direct conflict-of-interest rationale, but it is still an analysis piece rather than a formal finding.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: the concern arises specifically from Marcos's family history and administration.
contrary_evidence: It is an analyst view, not a formal legal finding.
Officials argued the agency had outlived usefulness.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
